advisory.finding: Both spy tests check which git subcommand was used, `("cat-file", "blob")`, instead of only what the restore produces. A fix that keeps the same behavior but takes a different route would break them, for example `git show <rev>:<path> --` (the `--` also stops the filename stat) or `cat-file -p`. On non-Windows runners this check on the mechanism is the only thing guarding against the regression.
merged_from: The per-uuid fallback test reaches the fallback by monkeypatching the private helper `fsck_restore._deleted_history` to return `{}`. That replaces a function inside the unit under test, so renaming or inlining the helper breaks the test even though behavior has not changed.
scenarios: Someone later fixes the same bug by adding `--` to `git show` or by using `cat-file -p`. Behavior is the same, but both tests go red.
